name: Persistence via Unauthorized User Creation or Privilege Escalation
description: Identifies a series of actions that involve the creation of an unauthorized user or privilege escalation through the manipulation of user accounts and system services (crontab or systemd). Attackers may leverage these activities to establish persistence on the system, often with elevated privileges, to ensure continued access after reboots or security cleanups.
note:
- User Creation Analysis: Review the process.args and process.name fields to see which user was created, and determine whether the user account creation was authorized.
- Crontab Modification: Investigate changes to crontab files, particularly any new scheduled tasks or unexpected command entries.
- Systemd or Crontab Abuse: Identify attempts to modify systemd units or scheduled jobs that persist through reboots.
- Privilege Escalation Review: Verify if privilege escalation techniques (e.g., setuid, sudoers file modifications) have been employed.
- System Logs Review: Look at logs around the time of the event to determine if this activity is part of a broader attack campaign.
- Assess Impact: Determine if this persistence is actively being used to retain access to the system and possibly move laterally.
false_positives: Administrative actions like adding new users for system management might trigger this rule. Confirm that the user creation is legitimate and related to authorized system maintenance tasks.
Misconfigurations in scheduled tasks could lead to false alerts, especially in non-production environments. Validate the crontab or systemd files in use.
Review of systemd unit files and scheduled tasks may show benign entries that need to be excluded based on your system's configurations.
query:
FROM "logs-*"
  metadata _id, _version, _index
| WHERE event.action == "proctitle"
  AND (
    (auditd.log.proctitle LIKE "*useradd*" AND auditd.log.proctitle LIKE "*-m*" AND auditd.log.proctitle LIKE "*/bin/bash*")
    OR (auditd.log.proctitle LIKE "*usermod*" AND auditd.log.proctitle LIKE "*sudo*")
    OR (auditd.log.proctitle LIKE "*bash -i*" AND auditd.log.proctitle LIKE "*/dev/tcp*")
  )
| KEEP @timestamp, host.name, auditd.log.proctitle, _id, _version, _index
| SORT @timestamp ASC
